docs.text: dot-cli Dotkernel component to build console applications based on laminas-cli , for any PSR-11 container. dot-cli is a wrapper on top of laminas-cli Documentation Documentation is available at: https://docs.dotkernel.org/dot-cli/. Badges Versions Version Status PHP Documentation 4.x Active 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6 https://docs.dotkernel.org/dot-cli/v4/overview/ 3.x Security fixes only 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 https://docs.dotkernel.org/dot-cli/v3/overview/ Upgrading from 3.x? Read the upgrade guide . Requirements PHP : 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 or 8.6 laminas/laminas-cli : >= 1.16 symfony/console and symfony/event-dispatcher : 7.4 or 8.x A PSR-11 container that reads factories and aliases configuration, for example laminas/laminas-servicemanager (require it in your application) Setup 1. Install package Run the following command in your application's root directory: composer require dotkernel/dot-cli 2. Register ConfigProvider Open your application's config/config.php and the following line under the DK packages comment: Dot\Cli\ConfigProvider::class, 3. Copy bootstrap file Locate file bin/cli.php in this package, then copy it to your application's bin/ directory. This is the bootstrap file you will use to execute your commands with. 4. Copy config file Locate in this package the following file config/autoload/cli.global.php then copy it to your application's config/autoload/ directory. This is the config file you will add your commands to, using the command name as the key: 'commands' => [ Dot\Cli\Command\DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME => Dot\Cli\Command\DemoCommand::class, ], The lock files are written to data/lock by default. Make sure the directory exists and is writable. Testing Using the command line, go to your application's root directory, then type the following command: php ./bin/cli.php The output should look similar to this, containing information on how to start using dot-cli: Dotkernel CLI 1.0.0 Usage: command [options] [arguments] Options: -h, --help Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command --silent Do not output any message -q, --quiet Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed -V, --version Display this application version --ansi|--no-ansi Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output -n, --no-interaction Do not ask any interactive question -v|vv|vvv, --verbose Increase the verbosity of messages: 1 for normal output, 2 for more verbose output and 3 for debug Available commands: completion Dump the shell completion script help Display help for a command list List commands demo demo:command Demo command description. As shown in config/autoload/cli.global.php , dot-cli includes a demo command demo:command that will help you understand the basics of creating a new command. For more information, see laminas-cli documentation . Setting up as a cronjob * * * * * php /var/www/vhosts/example.com/httpdocs/bin/cli.php demo:command -q or * * * * * cd /var/www/vhosts/example.com/httpdocs/bin && php ./cli.php demo:command -q Adapt the command to your specifications by replacing example.com with your domain name. The -q (or --quiet ) option suppresses normal output, but errors are still written to stderr, including the lock error shown when the previous run of the same command has not finished yet. Use --silent instead if you want no output at all. License MIT

docs.text: Lock Files When a command starts running, a lock file is created for that command. The lock file ensures that the same command would not run before the previous one is done. If a command was force stopped, locate the lock file in the configured directory and delete it to refresh the command. Configuration Inside config/autoload/cli.global.php under the FileLockerInterface::class key the file locker can be disabled and the location of the lock files can be changed. FileLockerInterface::class => [ 'enabled' => true, 'dirPath' => getcwd() . '/data/lock', ],

docs.text: Configuration Register ConfigProvider After installation, register dot-cli in your project by adding the below line to your configuration aggregator (usually: config/config.php ): Dot\Cli\ConfigProvider::class, Copy bootstrap file Locate file bin/cli.php in this package, then copy it to your application's bin/ directory. This is the bootstrap file you will use to execute your commands with. Copy config file Locate in this package the following file config/autoload/cli.global.php then copy it to your application's config/autoload/ directory. Add your commands under the commands key, using the command name as the key and the command class as the value: 'commands' => [ DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME => DemoCommand::class, ExampleCommand::DEFAULT_NAME => ExampleCommand::class, ], The key must be the name from the command's #[AsCommand] attribute. Keep the name in a DEFAULT_NAME class constant and use it in both places, see Usage . A string such as 'demo:command' also works. Do not use DemoCommand::getDefaultName() : Symfony Console 8 removed that method, and Symfony Console 7.4 reports it as deprecated. Command classes that are registered in the container are fetched from it. Command classes that are not registered are instantiated without arguments. Custom event dispatcher By default, the application uses a new Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\EventDispatcher . To use your own, register it in the container under the key Laminas\Cli\SymfonyEventDispatcher , the same key laminas-cli uses. The service must implement Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\EventDispatcherInterface . 'dependencies' => [ 'factories' => [ 'Laminas\Cli\SymfonyEventDispatcher' => MyEventDispatcherFactory::class, ], ], The 3.x key Dot\Cli\Factory\SymfonyEventDispatcher still works, but it is deprecated and will be removed in 5.0.
docs.title: Configuration

docs.text: Lock Files When a command starts running, it takes an exclusive lock on a lock file named after the command, for example command-demo-command.lock . While the lock is held, another run of the same command stops with exit code 1 and the message The file lock is being held by a different process . The lock is released when the command finishes. If the process is killed, the operating system releases the lock, and the next run starts normally. The lock file itself stays in the directory, which is expected: there is no need to delete it. The lock uses the command's real name, so its aliases and abbreviations share one lock. For example, while demo:command is running, demo:com is rejected too. Unknown commands are not locked. Configuration Inside config/autoload/cli.global.php under the FileLockerInterface::class key the file locker can be disabled and the location of the lock files can be changed. FileLockerInterface::class => [ 'enabled' => true, 'dirPath' => getcwd() . '/data/lock', ], The directory in dirPath must exist and be writable by the user that runs the commands. If it does not, every command fails with exit code 1 and a message like The lock directory "..." does not exist or is not writable. Create it before running commands: mkdir -p data/lock Errors Lock errors are written to the error output (stderr), and they are shown even with the -q ( --quiet ) option. Use --silent to suppress them.
docs.title: Lock Files

docs.text: Overview [!IMPORTANT] dot-cli is a wrapper on top of laminas-cli dotkernel/dot-cli builds a console application from your application's PSR-11 container. Commands are registered in configuration, and a file lock stops the same command from running twice at the same time. The factories only depend on psr/container , so the package works with any PSR-11 container that reads factories and aliases configuration, for example Laminas Service Manager.

docs.text: Upgrading from 3.x to 4.0 Version 4.0 keeps the 3.x configuration format and the public classes. Most applications only need to update the commands keys in config/autoload/cli.global.php and require laminas/laminas-servicemanager themselves. Changes that can break your code Change Symptom Fix PHP 8.2 is no longer supported Composer refuses to install 4.0 Use PHP 8.3 or newer, or stay on 3.x laminas/laminas-servicemanager is no longer required Class "Laminas\ServiceManager\ServiceManager" not found if your application relied on dot-cli to install it Run composer require laminas/laminas-servicemanager in your application DemoCommand::$defaultName was replaced by the DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME constant A subclass that reads static::$defaultName fails with Access to undeclared static property Read DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME The shipped config no longer uses DemoCommand::getDefaultName() as a key A config key such as DemoCommand::getDefaultName() fails with Call to undefined method on Symfony Console 8 Use the command name as the key, see below The event dispatcher service key is now Laminas\Cli\SymfonyEventDispatcher None yet: the old key still works, but it is deprecated Rename the service key, see below A service under the event dispatcher key must implement Symfony\Component\EventDispatcher\EventDispatcherInterface Dot\Cli\Exception\InvalidConfigException when the application is created Register a Symfony event dispatcher under that key Aliases and abbreviations of a command share its lock demo:com or an alias is rejected while demo:command runs This is intended. Give commands that must run in parallel their own names Lock errors are written to stderr and are shown with -q Cron output now includes The file lock is being held by a different process Use --silent , or redirect stderr A missing or unwritable lock directory throws Dot\Cli\Exception\RuntimeException Commands exit with code 1 and a message instead of a TypeError Create the directory, or disable the locker FileLocker::getLockFilePath() throws Dot\Cli\Exception\RuntimeException without a directory or a command name Code that called it too early gets an exception instead of a TypeError Set both values first The factories throw Dot\Cli\Exception\InvalidConfigException instead of Exception None for catch (Exception) : the new class extends it Optionally catch the new class, or Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface ApplicationFactory::__invoke() returns Dot\Cli\Application instead of Symfony\Component\Console\Application A subclass that overrides __invoke() with the old return type fails to compile Narrow the return type in your subclass The MESSAGE_* constants are typed ( public const string ) A subclass that redeclares one of them without a type fails to compile Add the string type to the redeclared constant Command keys Before: 'commands' => [ DemoCommand::getDefaultName() => DemoCommand::class, ], After: 'commands' => [ DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME => DemoCommand::class, ], The DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME constant replaces the DemoCommand::$defaultName property. A subclass of DemoCommand that reads static::$defaultName fails with Access to undeclared static property . Read DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME instead. If one of your own commands still sets protected static $defaultName , replace it with a DEFAULT_NAME constant and use the constant in the #[AsCommand] attribute. Symfony Console 7.4 and 8 do not read the property, so it no longer names the command. See Usage for an example. Event dispatcher Before: 'factories' => [ 'Dot\Cli\Factory\SymfonyEventDispatcher' => MyEventDispatcherFactory::class, ], After: 'factories' => [ 'Laminas\Cli\SymfonyEventDispatcher' => MyEventDispatcherFactory::class, ], The old key is checked after the new one, and will be removed in 5.0. Laminas Service Manager dot-cli only uses the PSR-11 container interface. If your application builds its container with Laminas Service Manager, add it to your application's requirements: composer require laminas/laminas-servicemanager Dot\Cli\ConfigProvider still returns the same factories and aliases , so no configuration change is needed.
docs.title: Upgrading

Give commands that must run in parallel their own names Lock errors are written to stderr and are shown with -q Cron output now includes The file lock is being held by a different process Use --silent , or redirect stderr A missing or unwritable lock directory throws Dot\Cli\Exception\RuntimeException Commands exit with code 1 and a message instead of a TypeError Create the directory, or disable the locker FileLocker::getLockFilePath() throws Dot\Cli\Exception\RuntimeException without a directory or a command name Code that called it too early gets an exception instead of a TypeError Set both values first The factories throw Dot\Cli\Exception\InvalidConfigException instead of Exception None for catch (Exception) : the new class extends it Optionally catch the new class, or Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface ApplicationFactory::__invoke() returns Dot\Cli\Application instead of Symfony\Component\Console\Application A subclass that overrides __invoke() with the old return type fails to compile Narrow the return type in your subclass The MESSAGE_* constants are typed ( public const string ) A subclass that redeclares one of them without a type fails to compile Add the string type to the redeclared constant
docs.title: Changes that can break your code

docs.text: Before: 'commands' => [ DemoCommand::getDefaultName() => DemoCommand::class, ], After: 'commands' => [ DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME => DemoCommand::class, ], The DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME constant replaces the DemoCommand::$defaultName property. A subclass of DemoCommand that reads static::$defaultName fails with Access to undeclared static property . Read DemoCommand::DEFAULT_NAME instead. If one of your own commands still sets protected static $defaultName , replace it with a DEFAULT_NAME constant and use the constant in the #[AsCommand] attribute. Symfony Console 7.4 and 8 do not read the property, so it no longer names the command. See Usage for an example.
docs.title: Command keys

docs.text: Before: 'factories' => [ 'Dot\Cli\Factory\SymfonyEventDispatcher' => MyEventDispatcherFactory::class, ], After: 'factories' => [ 'Laminas\Cli\SymfonyEventDispatcher' => MyEventDispatcherFactory::class, ], The old key is checked after the new one, and will be removed in 5.0.
docs.title: Event dispatcher

docs.text: dot-cli only uses the PSR-11 container interface. If your application builds its container with Laminas Service Manager, add it to your application's requirements: composer require laminas/laminas-servicemanager Dot\Cli\ConfigProvider still returns the same factories and aliases , so no configuration change is needed.
docs.title: Laminas Service Manager

docs.text: Usage Use src/Command/DemoCommand.php as an example when creating a new command. Set the name and description in the #[AsCommand] attribute: Symfony Console reads them from there, so a command does not need a configure() method to set them. Keep the name in a DEFAULT_NAME class constant, and use the constant in the attribute and in config/autoload/cli.global.php . Then the command name is written in one place only. DemoCommand also implements configure() to show where a command can be extended by chaining methods, for example setHelp() , addArgument() and addOption() . For the demo, its configure() sets the same name and description as the attribute. Values set in configure() override the attribute, so if you keep both in your own command, keep them identical. <?php declare(strict_types=1); namespace App\Command; use Symfony\Component\Console\Attribute\AsCommand; use Symfony\Component\Console\Command\Command; use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface; use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface; #[AsCommand( name: ExampleCommand::DEFAULT_NAME, description: 'Example command description.', )] class ExampleCommand extends Command { public const string DEFAULT_NAME = 'app:example'; protected function execute(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int { $output->writeln('Hello from app:example'); return Command::SUCCESS; } } Then register it in config/autoload/cli.global.php : 'commands' => [ App\Command\ExampleCommand::DEFAULT_NAME => App\Command\ExampleCommand::class, ], Running Using the command line, go to your application's root directory, then type the following command: php ./bin/cli.php demo:command
